record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: Let M_tilde be the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. Let BV(R) be the Banach space of real-valued functions on R of bounded total variation with norm ||f||_{BV(R)} = |f(-infinity)| + Var(f), where f(-infinity) is the limit of f(x) as x tends to -infinity. Is the map M_tilde: BV(R) -> BV(R) continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\widetilde M$ denote the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, defined for locally integrable $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$\widetilde Mf(x) = \sup_{\substack{I\ni x \\ I\text{ bounded interval}}} \frac{1}{|I|}\int_I |f(y)|\,dy.$$
Let $\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ be the Banach space of real-valued functions $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$ of bounded total variation, equipped with the norm
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})} = |f(-\infty)| + \mathrm{Var}(f),$$
where $f(-\infty) = \lim_{x\to -\infty} f(x)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(f)$ denotes the total variation of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$.

It is known that $\widetilde M$ maps $\mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$ into itself boundedly. Determine whether the map
$$\widetilde M : \mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{BV}(\mathbb{R})$$
is continuous.
artifact.status_search_result: The continuity of the one-dimensional uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator on BV(ℝ) was established in subsequent work titled "BV continuity for the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator" (Beltran–Madrid, J. Funct. Anal., 2021), resolving the question affirmatively.
